crop_profile.summary: Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) is an annual fruit crop thriving in warm, humid climates with 18-30°C temperatures, 60-80% humidity, and 500-1000 mm annual rainfall. It prefers loam soils, pH 5.5-7.0, good drainage, and high nitrogen. Drip irrigation, balanced NPK (10-10-10) and organic amendments boost yields of 60-90 t/ha. Major producers include China, India, USA, Turkey, and Egypt. Key challenges are late blight, early blight, Fusarium wilt, and pests like fruit worm, whitefly, and aphids. Proper irrigation, fertilization, timely harvest, and refrigerated storage ensure high-quality marketable fruit.

recommendation.recommendation: Apply nitrogen fertilizer to correct low soil nitrogen and support optimal tomato vegetative growth.
recommendation.justification: Soil analysis shows nitrogen at a low level, which is below the tomato crop's high nitrogen requirement. All other agronomic factors (temperature, humidity, pH, texture, organic carbon) are favorable, and NDVI indicates strong crop vigor. Correcting the nitrogen deficiency within the next three days will prevent yield loss and capitalize on the existing growth opportunities.
actions: Confirm current soil nitrogen status with a quick field test (e.g., nitrate test strips) to validate the reported low level.
Select a readily available nitrogen source suitable for drip fertigation (e.g., urea 46% N or calcium nitrate 15.5% N).
Calculate the application rate: aim for 120‑150 kg N ha⁻¹ split into two doses (50 % now, 50 % at first fruit set). Adjust based on field test results.
Apply the first dose immediately (within 3 days) using the existing drip irrigation system, ensuring uniform distribution and avoiding runoff.
Schedule the second dose for the onset of flowering (≈30 days after planting) to sustain fruit set.
Record the amount applied, date, and method in the farm log.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Restored nitrogen balance will enhance vegetative growth, improve leaf chlorophyll content, and increase tomato yield and marketable fruit quality, leading to higher profitability.
monitoring_plan: Weekly leaf chlorophyll readings (SPAD meter) – target >45 for healthy tomato foliage.
Re‑test soil nitrogen 2 weeks after the first application; adjust the second dose if levels remain low.
Monitor NDVI via satellite or drone every 2‑3 weeks; aim to maintain NDVI ≥0.75.
Observe plants for signs of nitrogen excess (dark green foliage, delayed fruit set) and adjust future applications accordingly.
